subject: Risk & Compliance
title: How Sanctions Work
description: Learn How Sanctions Work in one minute.

hook.text: Your company unknowingly sells to a sanctioned entity. The fine is $1 billion. Ignorance is not a defense.

buildup.text: Sanctions restrict trade, finance, and travel with targeted countries, entities, or people for foreign policy goals.

discovery.text: The US OFAC maintains the SDN list — thousands of sanctioned names that every company must screen against.

twist.text: Sanctions are extraterritorial. A European company using US dollars can be sanctioned by the US for trading with Iran.

climax.text: Sanctions compliance is complex, expensive, and constantly changing. But violations are devastating.

punchline.text: Sell to the wrong entity. $1 billion fine. You should have checked.

quiz.question: What makes US sanctions extraterritorial?
options: Non-US companies using dollars can be sanctioned for US-prohibited trades
Sanctions only apply to US companies
Sanctions require UN approval to be enforced
